_comment: Isolated close-tier reproduction #3 for #1616, drill mode, no combat. Places a 30-wide single-rank Cavalry block (frontage_override 30, so Unit._pivot_radius() -- and therefore Unit.terrain_clearance() = _pivot_radius() + soldier_body_radius() -- is huge) close enough to the default map's hill patch (Battle.TERRAIN rect (1150,380)-(1400,580), kind 'block' -- the only PathField block_rect on this map; the forest patch is kind 'slow', a speed zone that PathField never routes around) that PathField._segment_blocked's clearance-grown margin around the hill swallows BOTH the unit's own position and its move-order destination, marking the direct leg spuriously 'blocked' even though neither point nor the direct line is anywhere near the drawn terrain. Ordered via a plain rmb_click move (no enemy, no far tier) to isolate PathField.next_step's funnel-corner computation as the mechanism, per the 'construct scenarios to isolate the phenomenon' rule.
